newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares close at record high.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares close at record high.

text.p: Turkey's stock market index ended the day at a record closing high on Thursday as signs of a stabilising financial environment drew fresh funds into the market, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 index closed up 1.92 percent at 75,263.85, well above a previous all-time closing high of 74,730.36 in early July.

"I think the rally is going to gather further force. With the central bank in control of money, funds could flood into the market," said Atilla Yesilada, director of research at Global Securities in Istanbul.
Brokers said steady treasury bill and lira rates supported the rise in prices.

"Recently the grip of both the treasury and the central bank was felt in the markets. This delayed any financial crisis expected to erupt in September," said Nalan Erkarakas, assitant to the general manager at Kentbank.

Yesilada said concerns about domestic debt and fears of a sharp rise in interest rates over the winter have now eased following a successful beginning to the government's programme of issuing foreign-currency denominated debt.
"The benefits of this are now feeding through into shares," he said.
